excerpt: World Labs, Fei-Fei Li's spatial intelligence company, makes Marble, which turns text, images and video into 3D worlds. Marble's prices, its funding and the pending AMD deal.
content:
World Labs builds what it calls spatial intelligence: AI world models that perceive, generate and reason about three-dimensional worlds. Its first product, Marble, creates detailed 3D environments you can move through, edit and export from text prompts, images, videos, 360-degree panoramas or a rough 3D layout. Worlds can be expanded and combined, and exported as Gaussian splats or meshes for game engines and other 3D tools. A separate World API lets developers generate worlds in their own software.

The company was founded in 2024 by Fei-Fei Li, a Stanford computer scientist, with Justin Johnson, Christoph Lassner and Ben Mildenhall. Li is chief executive. It came out of stealth in 2024 with $230 million of funding that valued it at $1 billion, Bloomberg reported, and in January 2026 Bloomberg reported funding talks at about a $5 billion valuation.

Marble opened in beta in September 2025 and became generally available on 12 November 2025. It is used for entertainment and creative work and for building simulated environments to train robots.

On 28 September 2026 World Labs announced it is joining AMD. AMD agreed to buy the company in an all-stock deal valued at about $8.2 billion; Li is to join AMD as executive vice president and chief scientist. The deal is expected to close by the end of 2026, subject to regulatory approval, so World Labs remains independent until then and Marble's plans could change afterwards.

Marble has a free plan and three paid tiers billed monthly, with credits that each action uses up.

We have not used Marble for this page. It brings together Marble's own website and pricing page and reporting from the outlets linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from.

profile.summary_short: Spatial intelligence company whose Marble app generates editable 3D worlds

use_cases: Generating 3D scenes for games, film previsualisation and VR
Turning a photo or panorama into an explorable 3D world
Building simulated environments for robot training
Exporting splats and meshes into existing 3D pipelines

fit: game, VR and film creators who want 3D environments quickly
robotics teams that need varied simulated scenes
developers who want world generation through an API
not_fit: people who need precise CAD or architectural models
commercial users on a budget: commercial rights start on the Pro plan

pricing.intro: Marble's plans from its pricing page and documentation, in US dollars per month. Each action uses credits; a basic world from one image uses about 1,580 credits. The World API is billed separately with prepaid credits.

plans.name: Free
plans.detail: 7,000 credits a month, up to about 4 world generations; no exports

plans.name: Standard
plans.detail: 20,000 credits, up to about 12 worlds; splat exports and collider meshes

plans.name: Pro
plans.detail: 40,000 credits, up to about 25 worlds; textured mesh (GLB) export and commercial rights

notes: Paid plans can buy top-up credits.
Prices may change after AMD's acquisition closes.

items.name: Google DeepMind Genie
items.what: Google DeepMind's interactive world model research
items.difference: Generates playable worlds frame by frame rather than exportable 3D assets.

items.name: Luma AI
items.difference: Known for video generation and capturing real scenes in 3D.

items.name: NVIDIA Cosmos
items.what: World foundation models for physical AI
items.difference: Aimed at robotics and autonomous-vehicle developers.

items.name: Physical Intelligence
items.difference: Controls real robots rather than generating worlds.

pros: Multiple input types, from text to video
cons: Commercial rights need the Pro plan
Pending AMD acquisition adds uncertainty about the product's future

faq.a: Yes, there is a free plan with 7,000 credits a month, enough for about four worlds, but it cannot export. Paid plans run from $20 to $95 a month.
Fei-Fei Li, Justin Johnson, Christoph Lassner and Ben Mildenhall founded it in 2024. Li is the CEO.
Yes. AMD agreed on 28 September 2026 to buy World Labs in an all-stock deal valued at about $8.2 billion, expected to close by the end of 2026.

faq.q: What can I export from Marble?
faq.a: Standard adds Gaussian splat exports and collider meshes; Pro adds high-quality textured mesh (GLB) export and commercial rights.
